\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتادن} (ettefâq oftâdan)}{اتفاق افتادن (ettefâq oftâdan)}]{\fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتادن} (ettefâq oftâdan) — to happen}

\label{lesson:FA-C301-ettefaq-oftadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the moment that, then the Persian for by chance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتادن}}
\textbf{\fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتادن}} (\emph{ettefâq oftâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to happen\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دیشب} \fa{در} \fa{خیابان} \fa{ما} \fa{یک} \fa{اتفاق} \fa{عجیب} \fa{افتاد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dishab dar khiyâbân-e mâ yek ettefâq-e 'ajib oftâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night something strange happened in our street.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}an event falls\textquotedblright{}. Present stem \emph{oft-}: \emph{in ziyâd ettefâq mioftad} \textquotedblleft{}this happens a lot\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Che ettefâqi oftâd?} \textquotedblleft{}What happened?\textquotedblright{}

\begin{cousinweb}
The noun \emph{ettefâq} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ittifāq} (EtymDB). The verb \emph{oftâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to fall\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian, so the phrase is a Persian compound verb built on an Arabic noun.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ettefâq oftâdan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ettefâq oftâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ettefâq oftâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the moment that, then the Persian for by chance, then say \emph{ettefâq oftâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتادن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To happen\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{روی} \fa{دادن} (ruy dâdan)}{روی دادن (ruy dâdan)}]{\fa{روی} \fa{دادن} (ruy dâdan) — to occur, to happen (formal)}

\label{lesson:FA-C301-ruy-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for by chance, then the Persian for to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{روی} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{روی} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{ruy dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to occur, to happen (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{اتفاق} \fa{ساعت} \fa{ده} \fa{شب} \fa{روی} \fa{داد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In ettefâq sâ'at-e dah-e shab ruy dâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This happened at ten at night.
\end{quote}

Formal and common in the news. Literally \textquotedblleft{}to give a face\textquotedblright{}, to show itself. Present stem \emph{dah-}: \emph{ruy midahad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ruy dâdan} joins \emph{ruy} \textquotedblleft{}face\textquotedblright{} and \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}, both inherited Persian; EtymDB takes \emph{dâdan} back to the Indo-European root \emph{deh\textsubscript{3}-}, \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ruy dâdan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ruy dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ruy dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for by chance, then the Persian for to happen, then say \emph{ruy dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{روی} \fa{دادن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To occur, to happen (formal)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{به} \fa{وقوع} \fa{پیوستن} (be voqu' peyvastan)}{به وقوع پیوستن (be voqu' peyvastan)}]{\fa{به} \fa{وقوع} \fa{پیوستن} (be voqu' peyvastan) — to come about, to take place (formal)}

\label{lesson:FA-C301-be-voqu-peyvastan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to happen, then the Persian for to occur.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{به} \fa{وقوع} \fa{پیوستن}}
\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{وقوع} \fa{پیوستن}} (\emph{be voqu' peyvastan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to come about, to take place (formal)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{اتفاق} \fa{دو} \fa{سال} \fa{پیش} \fa{به} \fa{وقوع} \fa{پیوست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{In ettefâq do sâl pish be voqu' peyvast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This came about two years ago.
\end{quote}

Very formal: news and history writing. \emph{voqu'} \textquotedblleft{}occurrence\textquotedblright{} + \emph{peyvastan} \textquotedblleft{}to join\textquotedblright{}; present stem \emph{peyvand-}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{voqu'} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{wuqū'}, \textquotedblleft{}a falling, an occurrence\textquotedblright{}; EtymDB lists no entry. \emph{peyvastan} \textquotedblleft{}to join\textquotedblright{} is inherited from Middle Persian \emph{paywastan} (EtymDB). Literally \textquotedblleft{}to join with occurrence\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be voqu' peyvastan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{be voqu' peyvastan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{be voqu' peyvastan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to happen, then the Persian for to occur, then say \emph{be voqu' peyvastan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صورت} \fa{گرفتن} (surat gereftan)}{صورت گرفتن (surat gereftan)}]{\fa{صورت} \fa{گرفتن} (surat gereftan) — to take place, to be carried out}

\label{lesson:FA-C301-surat-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to occur, then the Persian for to come about.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صورت} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{صورت} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{surat gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to take place, to be carried out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{جلسه} \fa{دیروز} \fa{صبح} \fa{صورت} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Jalase diruz sobh surat gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The meeting took place yesterday morning.
\end{quote}

Formal, for planned actions. Literally \textquotedblleft{}to take form\textquotedblright{}. Present stem \emph{gir-}: \emph{surat migirad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{surat} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣūra}, \textquotedblleft{}form, image\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian, from the Old Persian root \emph{grab-} \textquotedblleft{}to seize\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{surat gereftan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{surat gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{surat gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to occur, then the Persian for to come about, then say \emph{surat gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{دوام} \fa{آوردن} (davâm âvardan)}{دوام آوردن (davâm âvardan)}]{\fa{دوام} \fa{آوردن} (davâm âvardan) — to last, to hold out}

\label{lesson:FA-C301-davam-avardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to come about, then the Persian for to take place.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{دوام} \fa{آوردن}}
\textbf{\fa{دوام} \fa{آوردن}} (\emph{davâm âvardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to last, to hold out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سقف} \fa{خانه} \fa{زیر} \fa{برف} \fa{سنگین} \fa{دوام} \fa{نیاورد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Saqf-e khâne zir-e barf-e sangin davâm nayâvard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The roof of the house did not hold out under the heavy snow.
\end{quote}

Literally \textquotedblleft{}to bring durability\textquotedblright{}. Present stem \emph{âvar-}: \emph{davâm miâvarad}; the negative past is \emph{davâm nayâvard}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{davâm} \textquotedblleft{}duration, lasting\textquotedblright{} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{dawām}; EtymDB lists the Arabic word, though not the Persian one. \emph{âvardan} \textquotedblleft{}to bring\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
